[Construction of the representation]#para:operatorAlgebras_constructionGNS
Step 1. The idea to construct $\MH_\omega$ is the following: by definition, $\MFA$ is a Banach space, and according to [ref:pro:operatorAlgebras_formFromState], the state $\omega$ may be used to define a semi-inner product $\bdot_\omega$ on $\MFA$, given for all $A, B \in \MFA$ by

[equation:eq:operatorAlgebras_statePreIP]
$$
\braket{A, B}_\omega \ce \omega(A^\ast B) \ .
$$

This is not positive-definite because $\braket{A, A}_\omega = \omega(A^\ast A) = 0$ does not, in general, imply that $A = 0$. (Indeed, this is only the case for a faithful state.) One has to factor out the set

[equation:eq:operatorAlgebras_GNSideal]
$$
\MFJ_\omega \ce \set{A \in \MFA \ : \ \omega(A^\ast A) = 0}
$$

in order for $\bdot_\omega$ to become a proper inner product on $\MFA / \MFJ_\omega$. It turns out that $\MFJ_\omega$ is a left ideal of the algebra $\MFA$ [cite:BR1], [cite:BärFredenhagen09].

For $A \in \MFA$, let $[A]_\omega \ce \set{A + B : B \in \MFJ_\omega}$ be the equivalence class of $A$ in $\MFA / \MFJ_\omega$. As usual, one defines a linear structure on this quotient by setting $[A]_\omega + [B]_\omega \ce [A + B]_\omega$ and $\lambda [A]_\omega \ce [\lambda A]_\omega$ which does not depend on the specific representatives of the classes. For all $A, B \in \MFA$, define

$$
\vbraket[\big]{[A]_\omega, [B]_\omega}_\omega \ce \braket{A, B}_\omega = \omega(A^\ast B) \ .
$$

This is an inner product on $\MFA / \MFJ_\omega$: it is well-defined because $\MFJ_\omega$ is a left ideal of $\MFA$ [cite:BR1], [cite:BärFredenhagen09], and it is positive definite since $\vbraket[\big]{[A]_\omega, [A]_\omega}_\omega = 0$ implies $\omega(A^\ast A) = 0$, hence $A \in \MFJ_\omega$ and $[A]_\omega = [0]_\omega$. Let $\MH_\omega$ denote the completion of $\MFA / \MFJ_\omega$ with respect to the norm induced by $\bdot_\omega$. It is well-known that this space is a Hilbert space [cite:Werner18], and that $\MH_\omega$ contains the quotient $\MFA / \MFJ_\omega$ as a dense linear subspace [cite:Werner18].

Step 2. The next step is to construct the representatives $\pi_\omega(A) \in \BO(\MH_\omega)$ for all $A \in \MFA$. First, define $\pi_\omega(A)$ on $\MFA / \MFJ_\omega$ by setting for all $B \in \MFA$:

[equation:eq:operatorAlgebrasGNSpi]
$$
\pi_\omega(A) [B]_\omega \ce [AB]_\omega \ .
$$

It holds that $\pi_\omega : \MFA \longto \BO(\MFA / \MFJ_\omega)$ is a well-defined $\ast$-homomorphism [cite:BR1], [cite:BärFredenhagen09]. From this and the fact that $\MFA / \MFJ_\omega$ lies dense in $\MH_\omega$, it follows that $\pi_\omega(A) \in \BO(\MFA / \MFJ_\omega)$ can be uniquely extended to a bounded linear operator on $\MH_\omega$ ([ref:thm:operators_BLT]); this operator shall be denoted by the same symbol. Hence, one obtains a $\ast$-representation $\pi_\omega : \MFA \longto \BO(\MH_\omega)$.

Step 3. It remains to construct a vector $\Omega_\omega \in \MH_\omega$ such that $\omega = \omega_{\Omega_\omega}$ [cite:BR1], [cite:BärFredenhagen09]. Define $\Omega_\omega \ce [\idm]_\omega \in \MH_\omega$. For all $A \in \MFA$, it follows that

$$
\braket{\Omega_\omega, \pi_\omega(A) \Omega_\omega}_\omega = \vbraket[\big]{[\idm]_\omega, \pi_\omega(A) [\idm]_\omega}_\omega = \vbraket[\big]{[\idm]_\omega, [A]_\omega}_\omega = \omega(\idm^\ast A) = \omega(A) \ .
$$

Furthermore, since $\pi_\omega(A) \Omega_\omega = [A]_\omega$ for all $A \in \MFA$, one obtains that $\pi_\omega(\MFA) \Omega_\omega = \MFA / \MFJ_\omega$. By the very construction of the Hilbert space $\MH_\omega = \clos_{\ndot_\omega}(\MFA / \MFJ_\omega)$, this shows that the set $\pi_\omega(\MFA) \Omega_\omega$ lies dense in the latter. Therefore, $(\MH_\omega, \pi_\omega, \Omega_\omega)$ is a cyclic representation of the $C^\ast$-algebra $\MFA$.

The following important theorem asserts that the representation constructed above is essentially unique [cite:BR1]. Motivated by an algebraic description of quantum theory, the theorem was originally obtained by in 1947 [cite:Segal47], building on the pioneering work of and [cite:GelfandNaimark43].

[Gelfand-Naimark-Segal construction]#thm:operatorAlgebras_GNS
Let $\MFA$ be a $C^\ast$-algebra and $\omega \in \SS(\MFA)$ be a state. Then there exists a cyclic representation $(\MH_\omega, \pi_\omega, \Omega_\omega)$ of $\MFA$ such that for every $A \in \MFA$, there holds $\omega(A) = \braket{\Omega_\omega, \pi_\omega(A) \Omega_\omega}_\omega$. This representation is, moreover, unique up to unitary equivalence.

## Proof [label:eq:operatorAlgebras_constructionUnitaryEquiv]

The existence of the representation $(\MH_\omega, \pi_\omega, \Omega_\omega)$ was proved above in [ref:para:operatorAlgebras_constructionGNS]. Hence, only uniqueness must be shown. To this end, assume that $(\MH_\omega^\prime, \pi_\omega^\prime, \Omega_\omega^\prime)$ is another cyclic representation for $\MFA$ such that $\omega = \omega_{\Omega_\omega^\prime}$. Define an operator $U : \MFA / \MFJ_\omega \longto \MFA / \MFJ_\omega^\prime$ by

$$
U \pi_\omega(A) \Omega_\omega \ce \pi_\omega^\prime(A) \Omega_\omega^\prime \quad (A \in \MFA) \ .
$$

Note that this mapping is clearly linear due to the linearity of $\pi_\omega$ and $\pi_\omega^\prime$, and it satisfies the following relation for all $A, B \in \MFA$:

$$
\vbraket[\big]{U \pi_\omega(A) \Omega_\omega, U \pi_\omega(B) \Omega_\omega}_\omega &= \vbraket[\big]{\pi_\omega^\prime(A) \Omega_\omega^\prime, \pi_\omega^\prime(B) \Omega_\omega^\prime}_\omega = \omega(A^\ast B) = \vbraket[\big]{\pi_\omega(A) \Omega_\omega, \pi_\omega(B) \Omega_\omega}_\omega \ .
$$

Hence, $U$ is an isometry (so in particular injective and well-defined) with dense domain $\pi_\omega(\MFA) \Omega_\omega \subset \MH_\omega$ and with dense range $\pi_\omega^\prime(\MFA) \Omega_\omega^\prime \subset \MH_\omega^\prime$. Therefore, it can be extended uniquely to a unitary operator $U : \MH_\omega \longto \MH_\omega^\prime$ ([ref:thm:operators_BLT]). Finally, for $A, B \in \MFA$ one computes using $U^\ast U = \id_{\MH_\omega}$ that

$$
\pi_\omega^\prime(A) \pi_\omega^\prime(B) \Omega_\omega^\prime &= U \pi_\omega(AB) \Omega_\omega = U \pi_\omega(A) U^\ast U \pi_\omega(B) \Omega_\omega = U \pi_\omega(A) U^\ast \pi_\omega^\prime(B) \Omega_\omega^\prime \ ,
$$

hence $\pi_\omega^\prime(A) = U \pi_\omega(A) U^\ast$ on the dense subspace $\pi_\omega^\prime(\MFA) \Omega_\omega^\prime$; by continuous extension, this identity holds true also on $\MH_\omega^\prime$ which shows that the two cyclic representations are unitarily equivalent.

## Definition: GNS-representation [label:def:operatorAlgebras_GNS]

Let $\MFA$ be a $C^\ast$-algebra and $\omega \in \SS(\MFA)$ be a state. The unique cyclic representation $(\MH_\omega, \pi_\omega, \Omega_\omega)$ constructed from $\omega$ in [ref:thm:operatorAlgebras_GNS] is termed or of $\MFA$ associated with $\omega$.

The following two corollaries can be obtained immediately from the GNS-construction. They concern states with additional properties, namely faithful and invariant states, and they will be needed later on. The second corollary is from [cite:BR1].

## Corollary [label:cor:operatorAlgebras_GNSfaithful]

Let $\MFA$ be a $C^\ast$-algebra and $\omega \in \SS(\MFA)$ be a state. If $\omega$ is faithful, then the GNS-representation $(\MH_\omega, \pi_\omega, \Omega_\omega)$ is faithful.

## Proof

By [ref:def:operatorAlgebras_representation], it has to be verified that $\pi_\omega$ is injective. To this end, let $A \in \ker(\pi) \subset \MFA$ be arbitrary. Then it follows that $\omega(A^\ast A) = \braket{\Omega_\omega, \pi(A^\ast A) \Omega_\omega}_\omega = \norm{\pi(A) \Omega_\omega}^2 = 0$, hence one may conclude that $A = 0$ because $\omega$ is faithful. This shows that $\ker(\pi) = \{0\}$.

## Corollary [label:cor:operatorAlgebras_unitaryInvariantState]

Let $\MFA$ be a $C^\ast$-algebra, let $\omega \in \SS(\MFA)$ be a state on $\MFA$, and let $\tau \in \Aut(\MFA)$ be a $\ast$-automorphism on $\MFA$ which leaves $\omega$ invariant, that is, $\omega\bigl(\tau(A)\bigr) = \omega(A)$ for all $A \in \MFA$. Then there exists a uniquely defined unitary operator $U_\omega : \MH_\omega \longto \MH_\omega$, where $\MH_\omega$ is the representation space of the cyclic representation $(\MH_\omega, \pi_\omega, \Omega_\omega)$ of $\MFA$, such that

$$
U_\omega \Omega_\omega = \Omega_\omega \tand U_\omega \pi_\omega(A) U_\omega^\ast = \pi_\omega\bigl(\tau(A)\bigr) \quad (A \in \MFA) \ .
$$

## Proof

This is a consequence of the uniqueness of the cyclic representation, applied to the representation $(\MH_\omega, \pi_\omega^\prime, \Omega_\omega)$ with $\pi_\omega^\prime \ce \pi_\omega \circ \tau$. Note, in particular, that [ref:eq:operatorAlgebras_constructionUnitaryEquiv] determines the unitary operator $U_\omega : \MH_\omega \longto \MH_\omega$ uniquely due to the fact that $\pi_\omega(\MFA) \Omega_\omega$ lies dense in $\MH_\omega$.

The following theorem, which was first obtained in [cite:GelfandNaimark43] and which is a cornerstone of $C^\ast$-algebra theory, shows that $\ast$-representations actually exist by combining the GNS-representation with the Hahn-Banach theorem. The proof can be found, , in [cite:BR1] or [cite:Werner18].

[Gelfand-Naimark; non-commutative version]#thm:operatorAlgebras_structureCStar
Let $\MFA$ be a $C^\ast$-algebra. Then there exists a Hilbert space $\MH$ such that $\MFA$ is isometrically $\ast$-isomorphic to a uniformly closed $\ast$-subalgebra of $\BO(\MH)$.

## Remark [label:rem:operatorAlgebras_concreteCStar]

In [ref:exa:operatorAlgebras_CStar] [ref:enu:operatorAlgebras_exaConcreteCstar], a concrete $C^\ast$-algebra was defined to be a uniformly closed $\ast$-subalgebra of $\BO(\MH)$, and it was shown that such an algebra is an abstract $C^\ast$-algebra in the sense of [ref:def:operatorAlgebras_CStar]. Conversely, the fundamental [ref:thm:operatorAlgebras_structureCStar] asserts that every abstract $C^\ast$-algebra is $\ast$-isomorphic to a concrete $C^\ast$-algebra. Therefore, combining these results, it follows that abstract and concrete $C^\ast$-algebras are equivalent notions.

#exa:operatorAlgebras_GNS

[env]

- #enu:operatorAlgebras_exaGNSC Let $\MFA$ be a commutative unital $C^\ast$-algebra. According to the commutative version of the Gelfand-Naimark theorem (see [cite:GelfandNaimark43] as well as [cite:BR1] and [cite:Werner18]), there exists a compact Hausdorff space $X$ such that $\MFA \cong C^0(X)$. Let $\omega \in \SS(\MFA)$ be an arbitrary state on $\MFA$. Then from the Riesz-Markov-Kakutani representation theorem [cite:Conway85], [cite:Werner18], one obtains a unique measure $\mu$ on the space $\bigl(X, \MB(X)\bigr)$ such that $\mu(X) = 1$ and $\omega = \omega_\mu$ ( [ref:exa:operatorAlgebras_states] [ref:enu:operatorAlgebras_exaMeasureState]), that is

$$
\omega(f) = \int\nolimits_X f \diff \mu \quad (f \in \MFA) \ .
$$

To obtain the GNS-representation $(\MH_\omega, \pi_\omega, \Omega_\omega)$ of $\MFA$, note that the ideal $\MFJ_\omega$ from [ref:eq:operatorAlgebras_GNSideal] is given by $\MFJ_\omega = \set{f \in \MFA \, : \, \int_X \abs{f}^2 \diff \mu = 0}$, and that the inner product $\bdot_\omega$ on $\MFA / \MFJ_\omega$ takes the form $\braket{f, g}_\omega = \int_X \ol{f} g \diff \mu$. Since this is the usual $L^2$-inner product, it follows that $\MH_\omega = L^2(X, \mu)$. According to [ref:eq:operatorAlgebrasGNSpi], the representation $\pi_\omega : \MFA \longto \BO(\MH_\omega)$ acts like $\pi_\omega(f) g = fg$ for $f \in \MFA$ and $g \in \MH_\omega$, that is, $\pi_\omega(f) = M_f$ is the multiplication operator with the function $f$. Finally, the vector $\Omega_\omega \in \MH_\omega$ is identified with the constant function $\1_X \in \MFA$. Thus, the GNS-representation of $(C^0(X), \omega_\mu)$ is given by

$$
\bigl(L^2(X, \mu),\, M_{\sbullet},\, \1_X\bigr) \ .
$$

- #enu:operatorAlgebras_exaGNSBO Let $\MH$ be a separable Hilbert space and $\MFA = \BO(\MH)$. Consider a state $\omega \in \SS(\MFA)$ given by a density matrix $\rho \in \DM(\MH)$ as in [ref:exa:operatorAlgebras_states] [ref:enu:operatorAlgebras_exaNormalState], that is,

$$
\omega(A) = \tr(\rho A) \quad (A \in \MFA) \ .
$$

Assume, for simplicity, that $\rho$ is invertible, , that $\omega$ is faithful. The more general case of singular $\rho$ is discussed, , in [cite:AJP06].

The pre-inner product $\bdot_\omega$ from [ref:eq:operatorAlgebras_statePreIP] takes the form

[equation:eq:operatorAlgebras_GNSBO]
$$
\braket{A, B}_\omega = \omega(A^\ast B) = \tr(\rho A^\ast B) = \tr\bigl((A \rho^{1/2})^\ast \, B \rho^{1/2}\bigr) = \vbraket[\big]{A \rho^{1/2}, B \rho^{1/2}}_HS
$$

for all $A, B \in \MFA$, where in the last step [ref:eq:operators_HSinnerProduct] was used. Note that since $\rho$ is trace-class, $\rho^{1/2} \in \HS(\MH)$ is a Hilbert-Schmidt operator, hence the above expression is well-defined because $\HS(\MH) \subset \BO(\MH)$ is an ideal ([ref:pro:operators_NOHS]). The left ideal $\MFJ_\omega$ from [ref:eq:operatorAlgebras_GNSideal] used in the GNS-construction is trivial since $\omega$ is faithful. Therefore, the GNS-representation space $\MH_\omega$ is given by the completion of $\MFA$ with respect to the norm induced by $\bdot_\omega$, the $\ast$-homomorphism $\pi_\omega : \MFA \longto \BO(\MH_\omega)$ can be defined by $\pi_\omega(A) B = AB$ for all $A, B \in \MFA$, and finally the vector representative of $\omega$ is given by $\Omega_\omega = \id_\MH \in \MH_\omega$.

Define the following linear and unitary mapping:

$$
U :
\begin{cases}
\begin{aligned}
\bigl(\MFA, \bdot_\omega\bigr) &\longto \bigl(\HS(\MH), \bdot_HS\bigr) \ , \\
A &\longmto A \rho^{1/2} \ .
\end{aligned}
\end{cases}
$$

The inverse $\inv{U} : \HS(\MH) \longto \MFA$ is given by $\inv{U} B = B \rho^{-1/2}$, and $U$ is an isometry by [ref:eq:operatorAlgebras_GNSBO]. Hence, by uniqueness of the GNS-representation ([ref:thm:operatorAlgebras_GNS]), one may identify $(\MH_\omega, \bdot_\omega)$ with $(\HS(\MH), \bdot_HS)$, the transformed $\ast$-automorphism $\wt{\pi}_\omega : \MFA \longto \BO\bigl(\HS(\MH)\bigr)$, $\wt{\pi}_\omega(A) = U \pi_\omega(A) \inv{U}$, still takes the form $\wt{\pi}_\omega(A) B = A B$ for all $A \in \MFA$, $B \in \HS(\MH)$, and the vector representative $\Omega_\omega$ of $\omega$ is transformed to $U \Omega_\omega = \rho^{1/2}$. Thus, the GNS-representation of $(\BO(\MH), \omega_\rho)$ is given by

$$
\bigl(\HS(\MH),\, M_{\sbullet},\, \rho^{1/2}\bigr) \ . \tag*{\qedhere}
$$

# Modular Theory in von Neumann Algebras

#ch:vonNeumann

This chapter is devoted to Tomita-Takesaki modular theory and related notions which have revolutionized both the purely mathematical study of von Neumann algebras [cite:StratilaZsido19] as well their applications to algebraic quantum field theory [cite:Borchers00], [cite:BuchholzFredenhagen23] and quantum statistical mechanics [cite:BR2]. First, [ref:sec:vonNeumann_TomitaTakesaki] introduces the modular data for $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras. This framework is then used to define the standard form representation in [ref:sec:vonNeumann_standardForm]. Building on that, [ref:sec:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperator] discusses relative modular operators and some of their properties. Finally, [ref:sec:vonNeumann_spatialDerivative] treats the spatial derivative which is a generalization of the relative modular operator.

The main sources are the recent book [cite:Hiai21] as well as [cite:BR1], [cite:OP04], [cite:Stratila20], [cite:StratilaZsido19].

## Tomita-Takesaki Modular Theory

#sec:vonNeumann_TomitaTakesaki

In this section, the modular theory of von Neumann algebras, which was developed first by in two unpublished notes in 1967 and then presented in a didactically enriched and mathematically extended version by in 1970 [cite:Takesaki70], will be outlined.

### $\sigma$-finite von Neumann Algebras

σ-finite von Neumann Algebras

For applications to mathematical physics, the following type of von Neumann algebras turns out to be particularly relevant [cite:BR1].

## Definition: $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra [label:def:vonNeumann_sigmaFinite]

A von Neumann algebra $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ is said to be iff any family $(P_i)_{i \in I} \subset \PO(\MFM) \setminus \{0\}$ of mutually orthogonal non-zero projections in $\MFM$ (that is, $P_i P_j = 0$ for all $i \neq j$) is at most countable.

$\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras are characterized by the following theorem [cite:BR1].

[Characterization of $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras]#thm:vonNeumann_characterizationSigmaFinite
Let $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ be a von Neumann algebra. The following assertions are equivalent:

[equiv]

- $\MFM$ is $\sigma$-finite;

- there exists a countable subset which is separating for $\MFM$;

- there exists a faithful normal state $\omega \in \NS(\MFM)$;

- $\MFM$ is isomorphic to a von Neumann algebra which contains a cyclic and separating vector.

## Example [label:exa:vonNeumann_BOnormalState]

Consider the von Neumann algebra $\MFM = \BO(\MH)$ over a separable Hilbert space $\MH$. Every normal state $\omega \in \NS(\MFM)$ is of the form $\omega = \tr(\rho \ \sbullet\,)$ for some $\rho \in \DM(\MH)$ ([ref:thm:operatorAlgebras_characterizationNormalStates]). Furthermore, in [ref:exa:operatorAlgebras_states] [ref:enu:operatorAlgebras_exaNormalState] it was mentioned that $\omega$ is faithful if and only if $\rho$ is invertible. One can proceed to show that such a state exists, , that $\MFM$ is $\sigma$-finite, if and only if $\MH$ is separable [cite:BR1].

### The Tomita Operator

#subsec:vonNeumann_TomitaOperator

Let $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra. According to [ref:thm:vonNeumann_characterizationSigmaFinite], there exists a cyclic and separating vector $\Omega \in \MH$, and thus the mapping $\MFM \owns A \longmto A \Omega \in \MH$ is a linear bijection. One may use it to transfer the algebra involution $\MFM \owns A \longmto A^\ast \in \MFM$, which is an isometry, to an operation $A \Omega \longmto A^\ast \Omega$ on $\MFM \Omega$ which is, in general, not an isometry. The analysis of this mapping is the starting point of Tomita-Takesaki modular theory.

[Construction of the Tomita operator]#para:vonNeumann_preclosedTomitaOperator
([cite:Hiai21])
Consider two anti-linear operators ( [ref:para:operators_antiLinear]) $S_0 : \MH \supset \dom(S_0) \longto \MH$ and $F_0 : \MH \supset \dom(F_0) \longto \MH$ with domains $\dom(S_0) \ce \MFM \Omega$ and $\dom(F_0) \ce \comm{\MFM} \Omega$; note that by assumption on $\Omega$ (see also [ref:pro:operatorAlgebras_cyclicSeparating]), both $S_0$ and $F_0$ are densely defined operators. For every $A \in \MFM$ and every $\comm{A} \in \comm{\MFM}$, define their action by

[equation:eq:vonNeumann_preclosedTomitaOperator]
$$
S_0 A \Omega \ce A^\ast \Omega \tand F_0 \comm{A} \Omega \ce (\comm{A})^\ast \Omega \ .
$$

$S_0$ and $F_0$ are closable anti-linear operators on $\MH$.

## Proof

From the definition [ref:eq:vonNeumann_preclosedTomitaOperator] and the properties of the Hilbert-space adjoint, anti-linearity immediately follows. Let $A \in \MFM$ and $\comm{B} \in \comm{\MFM}$ be arbitrary. One computes

$$
\braket{A \Omega, F_0 \comm{B} \Omega} &= \braket{A \Omega, (\comm{B})^\ast \Omega} = \braket{\comm{B} A \Omega, \Omega} \\
&= \braket{A \comm{B} \Omega, \Omega} = \braket{\comm{B} \Omega, A^\ast \Omega} = \braket{\comm{B} \Omega, S_0 A \Omega} \ .
$$

By the definition of the adjoint of an anti-linear operator ([ref:para:operators_antiLinear]), this shows that $A \Omega \in \dom(F_0^\ast)$ and $F_0^\ast A \Omega = S_0 A \Omega$; since $A \in \MFM$ was arbitrary, this is to say that $S_0 \subset F_0^\ast$. As the adjoint is always a closed operator ([ref:pro:operators_propertiesAdjoint] [ref:enu:operators_adjointClosed]), it follows that $S_0$ is closable. By reading the above chain of equations backwards, one sees that $F_0 \subset S_0^\ast$, hence $F_0$ is closable as well.

Consider the anti-linear operators

[equation:eq:vonNeumann_closedTomitaOperator]
$$
S \ce \ol{S_0} = \dadj{S_0} \tand F \ce S^\ast = S_0^\ast \ ,
$$

where the bar denotes the closure of the operator $S_0$, see [ref:para:operators_closure]. (Recall also [ref:pro:operators_propertiesAdjoint] [ref:enu:operators_adjointClosure] for the second identities in both definitions.) The operator $S$ is called the of the von Neumann algebra $\MFM$ with respect to the cyclic and separating vector $\Omega$, and it is also denoted by $S_\Omega$ or $S_\omega$ to emphasize the dependence on $\Omega$ or $\omega = \omega_\Omega$.

## Lemma [label:lem:vonNeumann_propertiesTomitaOperator]

The operator $S$ and its adjoint $S^\ast$ enjoy the following properties:

- $S$ is invertible with $\inv{S} = S$.

- The ranges of $S$ and $S^\ast$ lie dense in $\MH$

## Proof

[ref:enu:vonNeumann_Sinvertible]. By definition, it holds that $\ran(S_0) = \dom(S_0)$ and $S_0^2 = \id_\MH$. Therefore, $S_0$ is invertible with $\inv{S_0} = S_0$. From [ref:pro:operators_propertiesAdjoint] [ref:enu:operators_inverseClosure], it follows that $\inv{S_0}$ is closable with

$$
\inv{S} = \inv{(\ol{S_0})} = \ol{(\inv{S_0})} = S \ .
$$

[ref:enu:vonNeumann_ranSdense]. First, it will be shown that $\dom(S_0) \subset \ran(S)$. To this end, let $\xi \in \dom(S_0)$ be arbitrary, , $\xi = A \Omega$ for some $A \in \MFM$. Since $S$ is an extension of $S_0$, it follows that $\dom(S_0) \subset \dom(S)$ and $S B \Omega = S_0 B \Omega = B^\ast \Omega$ for all $B \in \MFM$. Thus, since $\eta = A^\ast \Omega \in \dom(S_0)$, one obtains $S \eta = S_0 \eta = A \Omega = \xi$, hence $\xi \in \ran(S)$.

To see that the range of the adjoint $S^\ast$ is dense in $\MH$ as well, first note that since $S_0$ is closable, it follows from [ref:pro:operators_propertiesAdjoint] [ref:enu:operators_closability] that $\dom(S_0^\ast) = \dom(S^\ast)$ is dense in $\MH$. Hence, one can use [ref:enu:operators_ranTperp] of the same proposition and the definition of $S$ to conclude that $\ran(S^\ast)^\perp = \ker(S^{\ast \ast}) = \ker{S} = \set{0}$ by assertion [ref:enu:vonNeumann_Sinvertible] proved above. From [ref:cor:operators_characterizationPerp] [ref:enu:operators_densePerp], the claim now follows.

[Polar decomposition of the Tomita operator]#para:vonNeumann_polarDecompositionTomita
One can compute the polar decomposition of the closed operator $S$ ( [ref:thm:operators_polarDecompositionCO]) to obtain a unique partial isometry $J : \MH \longto \MH$ and a unique positive self-adjoint linear operator $\Delta : \MH \supset \dom(\Delta) \longto \MH$ such that

[equation:eq:vonNeumann_modularOperator]
$$
S = J \Delta^{1/2} \twith \Delta \ce S^\ast S = F S \ .
$$

$J$ is an anti-linear unitary operator, and $\Delta$ is invertible.

## Proof

The operator $J$ is anti-linear and maps its initial space $\ker(S)^\perp = [\ran(S^\ast)]$ isometrically onto its final space $\ker(S^\ast)^\perp = [\ran(S)]$, and it satisfies $J \equiv 0$ on $\ker(S)^{\perp\perp} = [\ker(S)]$. From [ref:lem:vonNeumann_propertiesTomitaOperator], it follows that both initial and final space of $J$ are given by $\MH$, and that $\ker(S) = \set{0}$. Therefore, $J$ maps $\MH$ isometrically to $\MH$ and is thus a unitary operator [cite:Conway85]. To see that $\Delta = S^\ast S$ is invertible, note that from [ref:pro:operators_propertiesAdjoint] [ref:enu:operators_inverseAdjoint], it follows that $S^\ast$ is invertible with $(S^\ast)^{-1} = (S^{-1})^\ast$. Hence, $\Delta$ is invertible with $\inv{\Delta} = \inv{S} \inv{(S^\ast)} = \inv{S} (\inv{S})^\ast = S S^\ast$.

### Modular Data and Tomita's Theorem

#subsec:vonNeumann_modularData

The observations made in the previous [ref:para:vonNeumann_polarDecompositionTomita] motivate the following definition.

## Definition: Modular data [label:def:vonNeumann_modularData]

The operator $J$ is called the with respect to the von Neumann algebra $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ and the cyclic and separating vector $\Omega \in \MH$, and the operator $\Delta$ is called the with respect to $(\MFM, \Omega)$. To emphasize the dependence on the vector $\Omega$ or the functional $\omega = \omega_\Omega$, one also writes $J_\Omega, J_\omega$ and $\Delta_\Omega, \Delta_\omega$.

The next proposition contains some of the most important properties of the modular data; they will be used very often in the following discussions (sometimes implicitly). The proof is an elaborated version of [cite:Hiai21] with some insights from [cite:StratilaZsido19].

## Proposition [label:pro:vonNeumann_propertiesModularData]

Let $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ be a von Neumann algebra with cyclic and separating vector $\Omega \in \MH$, and let $(J, \Delta)$ denote the modular data with respect to $(\MFM, \Omega)$.

- $J^\ast = J$ and $J^2 = \id_\MH$.

- $\Delta = FS$ and $\inv{\Delta} = SF$.

- $S = J \Delta^{1/2} = \Delta^{-1/2} J$ and $F = J \Delta^{-1/2} = \Delta^{1/2} J$.

- $\inv{\Delta} = J \Delta J$ and $J \Delta^{\ii t} = \Delta^{\ii t} J$ for all $t \in \R$.

- $J \Omega = \Omega$ and $\Delta \Omega = \Omega$.

- If $f : [0, + \infty) \longto \C$ is Borel-measurable, then $f(\Delta) \Omega = f(1) \Omega$.

## Proof [label:eq:vonNeumann_funcCalcModOp]

Since $S = \inv{S}$ by [ref:lem:vonNeumann_propertiesTomitaOperator] [ref:enu:vonNeumann_Sinvertible] and $\inv{J} = J^\ast$ by [ref:para:vonNeumann_polarDecompositionTomita], it follows that

$$
S = J \Delta^{1/2} = \bigl(J \Delta^{1/2}\bigr)^{-1} = \Delta^{-1/2} \inv{J} = \Delta^{-1/2} J^\ast = J^\ast J \Delta^{- 1/2} J^\ast \ .
$$

From this relation, uniqueness of the polar decomposition, and the fact that $J^\ast$ is a partial isometry as well [cite:Schmüdgen12], one can conclude that $J = J^\ast$ and $\Delta^{1/2} = J \Delta^{- 1/2} J^\ast$. The first identity (together with $J^\ast = J^{-1}$) establishes [ref:enu:vonNeumann_propertiesJ], and from the second, one can conclude the first part of [ref:enu:vonNeumann_inverseModOp]: using that $\Delta^{1/2} = J \Delta^{-1/2} J$ and $J^2 = \id_\MH$, one computes

$$
J \Delta J = J (J \Delta^{-1/2} J) (J \Delta^{-1/2} J) J = \inv{\Delta} \ .
$$

Let $f : [0, + \infty) \longto \C$ be any Borel-measurable function. From the previous identity and [ref:lem:operators_funcCalcUnitaryConj] (together with the observation $J (\lambda \Delta) J = \ol{\lambda} J \Delta J = \ol{\lambda} \inv{\Delta}$, $\lambda \in \C$), it follows that

$$
\ol{f}(\inv{\Delta}) = J f(\Delta) J \ .
$$

In particular, using this relation with $f(t) \ce \ee^{\ii t}$, one obtains $J \Delta^{\ii t} = \Delta^{\ii t} J$ for all $t \in \R$ which completes the argument to establish [ref:enu:vonNeumann_inverseModOp].

Next, assertion [ref:enu:vonNeumann_deltaFS] was already established in [ref:para:vonNeumann_polarDecompositionTomita] by noting that $F = S^\ast$, [ref:eq:vonNeumann_closedTomitaOperator]. Similarly, [ref:enu:vonNeumann_modDataTomitaOp] is an easy consequence of [ref:eq:vonNeumann_modularOperator,eq:vonNeumann_funcCalcModOp]: $S = J \Delta^{1/2} = J \Delta^{1/2} J^2 = \Delta^{-1/2} J$ and $F = S^\ast = \Delta^{1/2} J = J^2 \Delta^{1/2} J = J \Delta^{-1/2}$. For assertion [ref:enu:vonNeumann_actionModDatOmega], first note that $S \Omega = F \Omega = \Omega$ by [ref:eq:vonNeumann_preclosedTomitaOperator], hence $\Delta \Omega = FS \Omega = \Omega$ by [ref:enu:vonNeumann_deltaFS]. With this observation, [ref:enu:vonNeumann_funcCalcModOp] follows from [ref:lem:operators_funcCalcEigenvalue]. Finally, using this and [ref:enu:vonNeumann_modDataTomitaOp], one obtains also the first relation in [ref:enu:vonNeumann_actionModDatOmega]: $J \Omega = \Delta^{1/2} S \Omega = \Delta^{1/2} \Omega = \Omega$.

The following theorem is the fundamental result of the modular theory in von Neumann algebras. The proof is very technical and involved, and thus cannot be reproduced here. For detailed arguments, see [cite:BR1], [cite:Hiai21], [cite:StratilaZsido19], [cite:Takesaki70], or [cite:Takesaki03].

[Tomita]#thm:vonNeumann_Tomita
Let $J$ and $\Delta$ be the modular data of a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ with cyclic and separating vector $\Omega \in \MH$. Then the following identities hold true.

- #enu:vonNeumann_Tomita1 $J \MFM J = \comm{\MFM}$.

- #enu:vonNeumann_Tomita2 $\Delta^{\ii t} \MFM \Delta^{- \ii t} = \MFM$ for all $t \in \R$.

## Definition: Modular group [label:def:vonNeumann_modularGroup]

Let $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ be a von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal state $\omega \in \NS(\MFM)$, and let $\Delta$ be the modular operator associated with $(\MFM, \omega)$. The one-parameter group $\R \owns t \longmto \sigma_t^\omega \in \Aut(\MFM)$ of $\ast$-automorphisms of $\MFM$, defined by

$$
\sigma_t^\omega(A) \ce \Delta^{\ii t} A \Delta^{- \ii t}
$$

for all $A \in \MFM$ and $t \in \R$, is called the of $(\MFM, \omega)$.

#exa:vonNeumann_modularData

[env]

- #enu:vonNeumann_exaModOpLInf ([cite:Hiai21]) Let $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ be a von Neumann algebra possessing a faithful normal finite $\omega \in \NF{\MFM}$, that is, a functional satisfying $\omega(AB) = \omega(BA)$ for all $A, B \in \MFM$. Assume that $\omega = \omega_\Omega$ for a cyclic and separating vector $\Omega \in \MH$. For all $A \in \MFM$, it follows that

$$
\norm{A \Omega}^2 = \braket{\Omega, A^\ast A \Omega} = \omega(A^\ast A) = \omega(A A^\ast) = \braket{\Omega, A A^\ast \Omega} = \norm{A^\ast \Omega}^2 = \norm{S A \Omega}^2 \ .
$$

This shows that the Tomita operator $S$ with respect to $(\MFM, \omega)$ is an isometry, hence also anti-unitary by [ref:lem:vonNeumann_propertiesTomitaOperator] [ref:enu:vonNeumann_Sinvertible]. Therefore, the modular data is given by

$$
J = S \tand \Delta = \id_\MH \ .
$$

Note that if $\MFM$ were a commutative von Neumann algebra and $\omega$ an arbitrary faithful normal state, the same result would follow because $\omega$ is automatically tracial. This discussion suggests that in a sense, the modular operator $\Delta$ measures the non-tracial character of the state $\omega$ on the algebra $\MFM$ [cite:BR1]. In particular, Tomita-Takesaki modular theory is trivial in the commutative case. (There has, however, been a suggestion of a of Tomita's theorem in the context of classical statistical mechanics [cite:Gallavotti76].)

- #enu:vonNeumann_exaModOpBO Let $\MH$ be a separable Hilbert space and $\MFM = \BO(\MH)$. By [ref:exa:vonNeumann_BOnormalState], there exists a faithful normal state $\omega$ on $\MFA$ which is represented by an invertible density matrix $\rho \in \DM(\MH)$ in the form $\omega(A) = \tr(\rho A)$ for all $A \in \MFM$. Furthermore, recall from [ref:exa:operatorAlgebras_GNS] [ref:enu:operatorAlgebras_exaGNSBO] that the GNS-representation space of $\MFM$ is given by $\MH_\omega = \HS(\MH)$, with Hilbert-Schmidt inner product $\bdot_HS$, on which $\MFM$ acts by multiplication, the GNS-vector representative of $\omega$ is $\Omega = \rho^{1/2} \in \MH_\omega$, and $\omega = \omega_\Omega = \braket{\Omega, \,\sbullet\ \Omega}_HS$. In this case, the modular operator is given by [cite:HollandsSanders18]:

[equation:eq:vonNeumann_exaModOpBO]
$$
\Delta X = \rho X \rho^{-1} \quad (X \in \MH_\omega) \ .
$$

To see this, note that $\MFM \Omega$ lies dense in $\MH_\omega$ by the GNS-construction, hence it suffices to check the identity on this subspace. Let $A, B \in \MFM$ be arbitrary. Then

$$
\braket{B \Omega, \Delta A \Omega}_HS &= \braket{B \rho^{1/2}, \rho A \rho^{-1/2}}_HS = \tr\bigl((B \rho^{1/2})^\ast \rho A \rho^{-1/2}\bigr) = \tr(\rho A B^\ast) \\
&= \omega(A B^\ast) = \braket{A^\ast \Omega, B^\ast \Omega}_HS = \braket{S A \Omega, S B \Omega}_HS = \braket{B \Omega, S^\ast S A \Omega}_HS \ .
$$

In the second to last step, the Tomita operator [ref:eq:vonNeumann_preclosedTomitaOperator] was introduced, and in the last step, the definition of the adjoint of an anti-linear operator was used ( [ref:para:operators_antiLinear]). It follows that $\Delta$, as given in [ref:eq:vonNeumann_exaModOpBO], agrees with the operator $S^\ast S$, hence, by uniqueness of the polar decomposition of the Tomita operator, $\Delta$ must be the modular operator.

## Standard Form Representation

#sec:vonNeumann_standardForm

For the discussion of the relative modular operator in the next [ref:sec:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperator] as well as the development of perturbation theory in [ref:ch:perturbationTheory], the theory of the standard form representation of von Neumann algebras is an indispensible tool. It was developed, independently, by [cite:Araki74a] and [cite:Connes74] for $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras in 1974, and generalized by [cite:Haagerup75] in 1975.

### Definition and Examples

#subsec:vonNeumann_standardFormDef

[Natural positive cone]#para:vonNeumann_NPC
([cite:Hiai21])
Let $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ be a $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra with cyclic and separating vector $\Omega \in \MH$. Denote by $\Delta$ and $J$ the modular data with respect to $(\MFM, \Omega)$, and let $j : \MFM \longto \comm{\MFM}$ be the anti-linear $\ast$-isomorphism defined by

$$
j(A) \ce J A J \quad (A \in \MFM) \ .
$$

([ref:thm:vonNeumann_Tomita] [ref:enu:vonNeumann_Tomita1] shows that the range of $j$ is indeed the commutant $\comm{\MFM}$.) The $\NPC$ in $\MH$ associated with $(\MFM, \Omega)$ is defined to be

[equation:eq:vonNeumann_NPC]
$$
\NPC \ce \clos_{\ndot} \! \set[\big]{A j(A) \Omega \ : \ A \in \MFM} = \clos_{\ndot} \! \set[\big]{A J A \Omega \ : \ A \in \MFM} \ .
$$

The set $\NPC$ displays a number of very useful intrinsic properties as well as relations to the modular data. The proof of the next proposition can be found, , in [cite:BR1] or [cite:Hiai21].

## Proposition [label:pro:vonNeumann_propertiesNPC]

The natural positive cone $\NPC \subset \MH$ enjoys the following properties:

- $\NPC = \clos_{\ndot}(\Delta^{1/4} \PE{\MFM} \Omega)$. In particular, $\NPC$ is a closed convex cone inside $\MH$.

- $J \xi = \xi$ for all $\xi \in \NPC$.

- $\Delta^{\ii t} \NPC = \NPC$ for all $t \in \R$.

- $A j(A) \NPC \subset \NPC$ for all $A \in \MFM$.

- If $f : \R \longto (0, + \infty)$ is a positive-definite function on $\R$, then $f(\log \Delta) \NPC \subset \NPC$.

- $\NPC$ is self-dual in the sense that $\NPC = \set{\eta \in \MH \, : \, \text{$ 0$ for all $ _MATH_1755@@.

## Definition: Standard form [label:def:vonNeumann_standardForm]

A quadruple $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ consisting of a von Neumann algebra $\MFM$ represented faithfully on a Hilbert space $\MH$, an anti-unitary involution $J : \MH \longto \MH$, and a self-dual closed convex cone $\NPC \subset \MH$ is called a of the von Neumann algebra $\MFM$ iff the following properties are satisfied:

[num]

- $J \MFM J = \comm{\MFM}$;

- $J A J = A^\ast$ for all $A \in \MFM \cap \comm{\MFM}$;

- $J \xi = \xi$ for all $\xi \in \NPC$;

- $A j(A) \NPC \subset \NPC$ for all $A \in \MFM$.

[ref:para:vonNeumann_NPC] and [ref:pro:vonNeumann_propertiesNPC] show that every $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebra can be represented in standard form. Regarding non-$\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras, proved the following theorem in 1975 [cite:Haagerup75]. (See also [cite:StratilaZsido19].)

[Haagerup]#thm:vonNeumann_existenceStandardForm
Every von Neumann algebra possesses a standard form representation.

#exa:vonNeumann_standardForm

[env]

- #enu:vonNeumann_exaStandardFormAbelian Let $(X, \Sigma, \mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space. The von Neumann algebra $\MFM = L^\infty(X, \mu)$ acts on $\MH = L^2(X, \mu)$ by multiplication ([ref:exa:operatorAlgebras_vonNeumann] [ref:enu:operatorAlgebras_exaLInf]), and this action is faithful. Moreover, by assumption there exists a measurable function $g : X \longto \C$ such that $g > 0$ and $\int_X g \diff \mu < + \infty$ [cite:Kallenberg17]. This gives rise to the faithful normal functional $\omega(f) \ce \int_X f g \diff \mu$ on $\MFM$ ( [ref:exa:operatorAlgebras_normalStates] [ref:enu:operatorAlgebras_exaNormalStateAbelian]) with cyclic and separating vector representative $h \ce \sqrt{g} \in \MH$.

In [ref:exa:vonNeumann_modularData] [ref:enu:vonNeumann_exaModOpLInf], it was shown that $J = S$ is given by the Tomita operator. Furthermore, it holds that $j(f) = J f J$ implements the $\ast$-operation on $\MFM$: for all $f, g \in \MFM$, one has

$$
J f J (g h) = J (f g^\ast h) = g f^\ast h = \ol{f} (g h) \ .
$$

Therefore, the natural positive cone [ref:eq:vonNeumann_NPC] is given by $\NPC = \clos_{\ndot} \set{\abs{f}^2 h \, : \, f \in \MFM} = L^2(X, \mu)_+$, and hence the standard form representation of $\MFM$ is [cite:Hiai21]

$$
\bigl(L^\infty(X, \mu),\, L^2(X, \mu),\, J \xi = \ol{\xi},\, L^2(X, \mu)_+\bigr) \ .
$$

- #enu:vonNeumann_exaStandardFormTypeI Let $\MH$ be a separable Hilbert space and $\MFM = \BO(\MH)$. This algebra acts faithfully on $\HS(\MH)$ by multiplication, and one can show that the standard form representation of $\MFM$ is given by [cite:Hiai21]

$$
\bigl(\BO(\MH), \HS(\MH), J A = A^\ast, \HS(\MH)_+\bigr) \ ,
$$

where $J : \HS(\MH) \longto \HS(\MH)$, $A \longmto A^\ast$, is given by the operation of taking adjoints, and $\HS(\MH)_+$ is the cone of positive Hilbert-Schmidt operators.

### Properties of the Standard Form Representation

#subsec:vonNeumann_standardFormProperties

The following proposition, proved in [cite:BR1] or [cite:Hiai21], concerns further geometric properties of the cone $\NPC$. Note the close analogy between the following result and [ref:pro:operatorAlgebras_propertiesPE] which characterized the cone $\PE{\MFA}$ of positive elements in a $C^\ast$-algebra $\MFA$.

## Proposition [label:pro:vonNeumann_geometricPropertiesNPC]

Let $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ be a standard form. The closed convex cone $\NPC$ satisfies $\NPC \cap (- \NPC) = \{0\}$. Furthermore, if $\xi \in \MH$ such that $J \xi = \xi$, then $\xi$ can be uniquely decomposed as $\xi = \xi_1 - \xi_2$, where $\xi_1, \xi_2 \in \NPC$ with $\xi_1 \perp \xi_2$. Finally, $\MH$ is linearly spanned by $\NPC$.

One can show that the data $(J, \NPC)$ does not depend on the choice of a cyclic and separating vector $\Omega \in \MH$, hence the objects $J$ and $\NPC$ are universal [cite:BR1], [cite:Hiai21]. Furthermore, the elements of $\NPC$ enjoy some special properties.

## Lemma [label:lem:vonNeumann_vectorsNPC]

Let $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ be a standard form. For any $\xi \in \NPC$, it holds that $\xi$ is cyclic for $\MFM$ if and only if $\xi$ is separating for $\MFM$.

## Proof

([cite:Hiai21])
Let $\xi \in \NPC$ be arbitrary. If $\xi$ is assumed to be cyclic for the algebra $\MFM$, then $\xi = J \xi$ is cyclic for $J \MFM J = \comm{\MFM}$, hence it is also separating for $\MFM$ by [ref:pro:operatorAlgebras_cyclicSeparating] [ref:enu:operatorAlgebras_separatingMcyclicCommM]. The other direction is proved analogously.

The following theorem, which is the main result of this section, establishes a relationship between the natural positive cone of a von Neumann algebra and the space of normal functionals. The proof can be found in [cite:BR1] or [cite:Hiai21].

[Correspondence between $\NF{\MFM}$ and $\NPC$]#thm:vonNeumann_vectorRepresentativesNormalStates
Let $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ be a standard form. For every $\varphi \in \NF{\MFM}$, there exists a unique vector $\xi \in \NPC$ such that $\varphi = \omega_\xi$. In fact, the mapping $\NPC \longto \NF{\MFM}$, $\xi \longmto \omega_\xi$, is a homeomorphism with respect to the norm topology on both spaces.

## Remark [label:rem:vonNeumann_cyclicSeparatingFaithful]

The inverse of the mapping $\NPC \longto \NF{\MFM}$ of the previous theorem will be denoted by $\NF{\MFM} \longto \NPC$, $\varphi \longmto \xi_\varphi$, and $\xi_\varphi$ will be called the of $\varphi$. Combining [ref:cor:operatorAlgebras_faithfulSeparating] and [ref:lem:vonNeumann_vectorsNPC], it follows that

$$
\forall \xi \in \NPC \quad : \quad \xi \ \text{cyclic} \ \iff \ \xi \ \text{separating} \ \iff \ \omega_\xi \ \text{faithful} \ .
$$

An important consequence of [ref:thm:vonNeumann_vectorRepresentativesNormalStates] is that all $\ast$-automorphisms of the algebra $\MFM$ are implemented by unitary elements from $\MH$. This will be a key technical tool for the investigations in [ref:ch:perturbationTheory]. The proof can be found in [cite:BR1] and [cite:AJP06].

## Corollary [label:cor:vonNeumann_unitaryReprAut]

Let $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ be a von Neumann algebra in standard form. Then there exists a unique unitary representation $\Aut(\MFM) \owns \alpha \longmto U(\alpha) \in \UO(\MH)$ of the group $\Aut(\MFM)$ of $\ast$-automorphisms of the von Neumann algebra $\MFM$ on the Hilbert space $\MH$ such that

[num]

- $U(\alpha) \MFM U(\alpha)^\ast = \MFM$ and $U(\alpha) \comm{\MFM} U(\alpha)^\ast = \comm{\MFM}$;

- $U(\alpha) \NPC \subset \NPC$;

- $\forall A \in \MFM \, : \, \alpha(A) = U(\alpha) A U(\alpha)^\ast$;

- $\forall \varphi \in \NF{\MFM} \, : \, U(\alpha)^\ast \xi_\varphi = \xi_{\varphi \circ \alpha}$;

- $[U(\alpha), J] = 0$.

Furthermore, the mapping $\Aut(\MFM) \owns \alpha \longmto U(\alpha) \in \UO(\MH)$ is a homeomorphism when both spaces are equipped with the norm topology.

The final result of this section establishes uniqueness of the standard form representation up to unitary equivalence [cite:Hiai21].

## Corollary [label:cor:vonNeumann_uniquenessStandardForm]

Let $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ and $(\wt{\MFM}, \wt{\MH}, \wt{J}, \wt{\NPC})$ be two standard forms of von Neumann algebras $\MFM$ and $\wt{\MFM}$, respectively. If $\Phi : \MFM \longto \wt{\MFM}$ is a $\ast$-isomorphism, then there exists a uniquely defined unitary operator $U : \MH \longto \wt{\MH}$ such that

[label= ( *)]

- $\forall A \in \MFM \, : \, \Phi(A) = U A U^\ast$;

- $\wt{J} = U J U^\ast$;

- $\wt{\NPC} = U \NPC$.

## Relative Modular Operators

#sec:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperator

The construction of the modular operator with respect to a von Neumann algebra $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ and a cyclic and separating vector $\Omega \in \MH$ can be generalized to the situation in which two (not necessarily faithful) positive normal functionals $\varphi, \psi \in \NF{\MFM}$ are given. The resulting object can be seen as a non-commutative Radon-Nikodým derivative of these functionals [cite:Hiai21]; it was invented by [cite:Araki76, Araki77] who used it to extend the notion of relative entropy to general von Neumann algebras.

### Construction

Let $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ be a standard form and $\varphi, \psi \in \NF{\MFM}$. According to [ref:thm:vonNeumann_vectorRepresentativesNormalStates], there exist vectors $\Phi, \Psi \in \NPC$ such that $\varphi = \omega_\Phi$ and $\psi = \omega_\Psi$. Recall from [ref:pro:operatorAlgebras_supportVectorFunctional] that the support projections of the functionals $\omega_\Phi$ on $\MFM$ and $\comm{\omega_\Phi}$ on $\comm{\MFM}$ are given by $[\comm{\MFM} \Phi]$ and $[\MFM \Phi]$, respectively. In this and the subsequent chapters, the following notations shall be used:

[equation:eq:vonNeumann_supportProjectionsMT]
$$
\ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) \equiv \ssupp_\varphi \equiv \ssupp_\Phi \ce [\comm{\MFM} \Phi] \tand \ssupp_{\comm{\MFM}}(\varphi) \equiv \comm{\ssupp_\varphi} \equiv \comm{\ssupp_\Phi} \ce [\MFM \Phi] \ .
$$

## Lemma [label:lem:vonNeumann_commMsupport]

$J \, \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) J = \ssupp_{\comm{\MFM}}(\varphi)$.

## Proof

([cite:Hiai21])
Since the Hilbert space $\MH$ is linearly spanned by the natural positive cone $\NPC$ ([ref:pro:vonNeumann_geometricPropertiesNPC]) and since $J \xi = \xi$ for all $\xi \in \NPC$ ([ref:def:vonNeumann_standardForm]), it follows that $J \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) J \MH = J \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) \MH$. Using that $J \comm{\MFM} J = \MFM$ one obtains

$$
J \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) J \MH &= J \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) \MH = \clos_{\ndot}(J \comm{\MFM} \Phi) \\
&= \clos_{\ndot}(J \comm{\MFM} J \Phi) = \clos_{\ndot}(\MFM \Phi) = \ssupp_{\comm{\MFM}}(\varphi) \MH \ . \tag*{\qedhere}
$$

[The relative Tomita operator]#para:vonNeumann_relativeTomita
([cite:Hiai21])
For every pair of positive normal functionals $\varphi, \psi \in \NF{\MFM}$, define two operators $S_{\psi, \varphi}^0 : \MH \supset \dom(S_{\psi, \varphi}^0) \longto \MH$ and $F_{\psi, \varphi}^0 : \MH \supset \dom(F_{\psi, \varphi}^0) \longto \MH$ by

[equation:eq:vonNeumann_relativeTomitaOperator]
$$
S_{\psi, \varphi}^0(A \Phi + \eta) \ce \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) A^\ast \Psi \tand F_{\psi, \varphi}^0(\comm{A} \Phi + \zeta) \ce \ssupp_{\comm{\MFM}}(\varphi) (\comm{A})^\ast \Psi
$$

for all $A \in \MFM$, $\comm{A} \in \comm{\MFM}$, $\eta \in (\id_\MH - \comm{\ssupp_\varphi}) \MH$ and $\zeta \in (\id_\MH - \ssupp_\varphi) \MH$. Since $\id_\MH - \comm{\ssupp_\varphi}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $[\MFM \Phi]^\perp$ and $\id_\MH - \ssupp_\varphi$ onto $[\comm{\MFM} \Phi]^\perp$ ([ref:thm:operators_orthogonalProjection]), it follows that

$$
\dom(S_{\psi, \varphi}^0) = \MFM \Phi + [\MFM \Phi]^\perp \tand \dom(F_{\psi, \varphi}^0) = \comm{\MFM} \Phi + [\comm{\MFM} \Phi]^\perp \ .
$$

The operators $S_{\psi, \varphi}^0$ and $F_{\psi, \varphi}^0$ are well-defined anti-linear operators. Moreover, their domains lie dense in $\MH$, and they are closable.

## Proof

([cite:Hiai21])
. Let $A_i \in \MFM$ and $\eta_i \in [\MFM \Phi]^\perp$, $i \in \set{1, 2}$, be arbitrary such that $A_1 \Phi + \eta_1 = A_2 \Phi + \eta_2$. Observe that $(A_1 - A_2) \Phi = \eta_2 - \eta_1 \in [\MFM \Phi] \cap [\MFM \Phi]^\perp = \set{0}$, hence $A_1 \Phi = A_2 \Phi$. By definition of $\ssupp_\MFM(\varphi)$, this implies $A_1 \, \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) = A_2 \, \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi)$ on $\MH$. In particular, one may conclude that $\ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) A_1^\ast \Psi = \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) A_2^\ast \Psi$. Thus,

$$
S_{\psi, \varphi}^0 (A_1 \Phi + \eta_1) = \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) A_1^\ast \Psi = \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) A_2^\ast \Psi = S_{\psi, \varphi}^0 (A_2 \Phi + \eta_2)
$$

which shows that the operator $S_{\psi, \varphi}^0$ is well-defined; an analogous argument establishes the same for the operator $F_{\psi, \varphi}^0$.

. It holds that $\MH \supset \clos_{\ndot} \dom(S_{\psi, \varphi}^0) = \clos_{\ndot}(\MFM \Phi + [\MFM \Phi]^\perp) \supset \clos_{\ndot}(\MFM \Phi) + \clos_{\ndot}([\MFM \Phi]^\perp) = [\MFM \Phi] + [\MFM \Phi]^\perp = \MH$ ( [ref:thm:operators_orthogonalProjection] and note that the orthogonal complement is always closed). This shows that $S_{\psi, \varphi}^0$ is densely defined; for the operator $F_{\psi, \varphi}^0$ defined on $\comm{\MFM} \Phi + [\comm{\MFM} \Phi]^\perp$, the argument is analogous. The anti-linearity of these operators is clear from their definition.

. Let $A \in \MFM$, $\eta \in [\MFM \Phi]^\perp$ and $\comm{A} \in \comm{\MFM}$, $\zeta \in [\comm{\MFM} \Phi]^\perp$ be arbitrary. One computes

$$
\vbraket[\big]{A \Phi + \eta, F_{\psi, \varphi}^0 (\comm{A} \Phi + \zeta)} &= \vbraket[\big]{A \Phi + \eta, \ssupp_{\comm{\MFM}}(\varphi) (\comm{A})^\ast \Psi} = \vbraket[\big]{A \Phi, (\comm{A})^\ast \Psi} = \vbraket[\big]{\comm{A} \Phi, A^\ast \Psi} \\
&= \vbraket[\big]{\ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) (\comm{A} \Phi + \zeta), A^\ast \Psi} = \vbraket[\big]{\comm{A} \Phi + \zeta, \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) A^\ast \Psi} \\
&= \vbraket[\big]{\comm{A} \Phi + \zeta, S_{\psi, \varphi}^0(A \Phi + \eta)} \ .
$$

From the definition of the adjoint of an anti-linear operator ([ref:para:operators_antiLinear]), it follows that $S_{\psi, \varphi}^0 \subset (F_{\psi, \varphi}^0)^\ast$ and $F_{\psi, \varphi}^0 \subset (S_{\psi, \varphi}^0)^\ast$, hence [ref:pro:operators_propertiesAdjoint] shows that both $S_{\psi, \varphi}^0$ and $F_{\psi, \varphi}^0$ are closable.

Let $S_{\psi, \varphi}$ and $F_{\psi, \varphi}$ denote the closures of the operators $S_{\psi, \varphi}^0$ and $F_{\psi, \varphi}^0$, respectively. One refers to $S_{\psi, \varphi}$ as the associated with the functionals $\varphi, \psi \in \NF{\MFM}$. If $\psi = \varphi$, one simply writes $S_\varphi$ and $F_\varphi$ for these operators. Note that if $\psi = \varphi$ is faithful, then $S_\varphi$ agrees with the Tomita operator defined in [ref:para:vonNeumann_preclosedTomitaOperator]: indeed, the vector representative $\Phi$ of $\varphi$ is cyclic and separating ([ref:rem:vonNeumann_cyclicSeparatingFaithful]), hence $[\MFM \Phi] = \MH$ and $[\MFM \Phi]^\perp = \{0\}$ so that $S_\varphi^0 A \Phi = A^\ast \Phi = S A \Phi$ for all $A \in \MFM$.

## Definition: Relative modular operator [label:def:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperator]

The $\Delta_{\psi, \varphi}$ with respect to the positive normal functionals $\psi$ and $\varphi$ on $\MFM$ is defined to be

$$
\Delta_{\psi, \varphi} \ce S_{\psi, \varphi}^\ast S_{\psi, \varphi} \ .
$$

In the case that $\psi = \varphi$, one simply writes $\Delta_\varphi$ for $\Delta_{\varphi, \varphi}$ and calls this the of $\varphi$. (Note that by the above remark, it holds that if $\varphi$ is faithful, then $\Delta_\varphi$ agrees with the operator $\Delta$ from [ref:def:vonNeumann_modularData].) One also writes

$$
\Delta_{\Psi, \Phi} \equiv \Delta_{\psi, \varphi} \tand S_{\Psi, \Phi} \equiv S_{\psi, \phi} \ .
$$

The following examples [cite:Hiai21] shed some light on the abstract concept of the relative modular operator. Note, in particular, that [ref:enu:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperatorAbelian] shows that this concept is non-trivial for commutative von Neumann algebras which is in contrast to the situation for the modular operator found in [ref:exa:vonNeumann_modularData] [ref:enu:vonNeumann_exaModOpLInf].

#exa:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperator

[env]

- #enu:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperatorAbelian Let $(X, \Sigma, \mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space and $\MFM = L^\infty(X, \mu)$, acting on $\MH = L^2(X, \mu)$. Recall from [ref:exa:operatorAlgebras_normalStates] [ref:enu:operatorAlgebras_exaNormalStateAbelian] that there is a one-to-one correspondence $\NF{\MFM} \cong L^1(X, \mu)_+$; in particular, every $\psi \in \NF{\MFM}$ gives rise to a measure $\diff \nu_\psi = h_\psi \diff \mu$. For every pair of normal functionals $\varphi, \psi \in \NF{\MFM}$, it holds that the relative modular operator $\Delta_{\psi, \varphi}$ is given by the multiplication operator with the function

$$
\1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}} \cdot \frac{h_\psi}{h_\varphi} \ .
$$

To see this, let $f, g \in \MFM$ be arbitrary and note that the vector representative of $\varphi$ in the natural positive cone is $\Phi \ce \sqrt{h_\varphi} \in L^2(X, \mu)_+$. The support projection of $\varphi$ is given by $\ssupp_\MFM(\varphi) = \1_{\set{\varphi > 0}} = \1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}}$. Indeed, if there were $P \in \PO(\MFM)$ such that $\varphi(P) = \varphi(\1_X)$ and $P < \ssupp_\MFM(\varphi)$, then

$$
\int_X h_\varphi \diff \mu = \varphi(\1_X) = \varphi(P) = \int_X P h_\varphi \diff \mu < \int_X \1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}} h_\varphi \diff \mu = \int_X h_\varphi \diff \mu \ ,
$$

a contradiction. Since $\MFM$ is commutative, it holds that $\ssupp_{\comm{\MFM}}(\varphi) = \1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}}$ as well. Let $\eta, \zeta \in (\1_X - \comm{\ssupp_\varphi}) \MH$ be arbitrary, and observe that $\1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}} \eta = \1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}} \zeta = 0$. One then computes

$$
\vbraket[\big]{f \, \Phi + \eta, \Delta_{\psi, \varphi} (g \, \Phi + \zeta)} &= \int\nolimits_X \ol{(f \, \Phi + \eta)} \, \1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}} \, \frac{h_\psi}{h_\varphi} \, (g \, \Phi + \zeta) \diff \mu = \int\nolimits_X \1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}} \ol{f} g h_\psi \diff \mu \\
&= \vbraket[\big]{\1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}} \ol{g} \, \Psi, \1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}} \ol{f} \, \Psi} = \vbraket[\big]{S_{\psi, \varphi} (g \, \Phi + \zeta), S_{\psi, \varphi} (f \, \Phi + \eta)} \
$$
5pt]
&= f \, + , S_ , ^ S_ , (g \, + ) \ ,
$$

where $\Psi \ce \sqrt{h_\psi} \in L^2(X, \mu)_+$ is the vector representative of $\psi$. From the uniqueness of the polar decomposition of the relative Tomita operator, the claim now follows.

It holds that $\Delta_{\psi, \varphi} = \1_{\set{h_\varphi > 0}} \, \frac{h_\psi}{h_\varphi}$ is equal to the Radon-Nikodým derivative $\od{\nu_\psi}{\nu_\varphi}$ of the measure $\diff \nu_\psi = h_\psi \diff \mu$ with respect to the measure $\diff \nu_\varphi = h_\varphi \diff \mu$. (This is the reason for calling the relative modular operator a non-commutative Radon-Nikodým derivative.) Indeed, for all $A \in \Sigma$, one easily computes that

$$
_ (A) = _A h_ = _A \1_ \, h_ \, h_ = _A \1_ \, h_ _ \ .
$$

- {#enu:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperatorTypeI} Let $\MH$ be a separable Hilbert space. Consider the von Neumann algebra $\MFM = \BO(\MH)$ which is represented in standard form on the Hilbert space $\HS(\MH)$ ([ref:exa:vonNeumann_standardForm] [ref:enu:vonNeumann_exaStandardFormTypeI]). ### Properties of Relative Modular Operators

{#subsec:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperatorProperties}

The most important properties of the relative modular operator are contained in the next proposition whose proof shall be skipped as it is quite involved; see [cite:Hiai21].

## Proposition [label:pro:vonNeumann_propertiesRelativeModularOp]

Let $\psi, \varphi \in \NF{\MFM}$ be two positive normal functionals on a von Neumann algebra $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ in standard form.

- The support projection (\cf{} [ref:para:operators_supportPO]) of the relative modular operator $\Delta_{\psi, \varphi}$ is

$$
( _ , ) = _ ( ) \, _ ( ) = _ ( ) J _ ( ) J \ .
$$

- The polar decomposition of $S_{\psi, \varphi}$ takes the form $S_{\psi, \varphi} = J \Delta_{\psi, \varphi}^{1/2}$.

- The inverse operator $\Delta_{\varphi, \psi}^{-1}$, defined on the support of $\Delta_{\varphi, \psi}$, is given by $\Delta_{\varphi, \psi}^{-1} = J \Delta_{\psi, \varphi} J$.

The next two lemmata will be useful for arguments in the following chapters. These properties are mentioned, for example, in [cite:DJP03]. Let again $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ be a von Neumann algebra in standard form and $\varphi, \psi \in \NF{\MFM}$.

## Lemma [label:lem:vonNeumann_relModOpCommutesCenter]

If $B \in \MFM \cap \comm{\MFM}$ belongs to the center of $\MFM$, then $B$ commutes with $\Delta_{\varphi, \psi}$.

## Proof

Let $A, C \in \MFM$ and $\eta, \zeta \in [\MFM \Psi]^\perp$ be arbitrary. Then

$$
C + , _ , B (A + ) &= S_ , B (A + ), S_ , (C + ) \\
&= \\

&= S_ , (A + ), S_ , (B^ C + B^ ) \\
&= C + , B _ , (A + ) \ .
$$

First, the definition of the adjoint of an anti-linear operator was employed ([ref:para:operators_antiLinear]). In the second line, it was used that $\eta \in [\MFM \Psi]^\perp = \ker(\comm{\ssupp_\psi})$ implies $\ssupp_{\comm{\MFM}}(\psi) B \eta = B \, \ssupp_{\comm{\MFM}}(\psi) \eta = 0$, which shows that $B \eta \in \ker(\comm{\ssupp_\psi})$. Since the space $\MFM \Psi + [\MFM \Psi]^\perp$ lies dense in $\MH$, the claim follows from the above identity.

The following result is also standard in modular theory; it can be found, for example, in [cite:Araki77], and the proof given below is a more detailed version of the one given in this reference.

## Lemma [label:lem:vonNeumann_relativeModularOpUnitary]

Let $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ be a von Neumann algebra in standard form, let $\varphi, \psi \in \NF{\MFM}$ be positive normal functionals with vector representatives $\Phi, \Psi \in \NPC$, and let $U \in \UO(\MH)$ be a unitary operator such that $U A U^\ast = A$ for all $A \in \MFM$ and $U \NPC \subset \NPC$. Then

$$

$$

This section shall be concluded with a result concerning convergence properties of the relative modular operator which will be used in the perturbation theory of KMS-states in [ref:ch:perturbationTheory]. The proof presented below is a more detailed version of [cite:DJP03].

## Lemma [label:lem:vonNeumann_convergenceRelModOp]

Let $\MFM$ be a von Neumann algebra represented in standard form $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$, and let $(\Phi_n)_{n \in \N} \subset \NPC$ and $(\Psi_n)_{n \in \N} \subset \NPC$ be two sequences. Assume that the following properties are satisfied:

[cond]

- $\Delta_{\Phi_n, \Psi_n} \to M$ in the strong resolvent sense ([ref:def:operators_SRConvergence]);

- $\ssupp_{\Psi_n} \to \ssupp_\Psi$ in the strong operator topology;

- $\Phi_n \to \Phi$ weakly in $\MH$;

- $\Psi_n \to \Psi$ weakly in $\MH$.

Then it follows that $M = \Delta_{\Phi, \Psi}$.

Let $A \in \MFM$ be arbitrary. $$

$$

Finally, it holds that $\Delta_{\Phi_n, \Psi_n}^{1/2} \to M^{1/2}$ in the strong resolvent sense by [ref:lem:operators_SRimpliesFSR] and assumption [ref:enu:vonNeumann_convergenceRelModOpA1].

Therefore, applying [ref:pro:operators_SRimpliesW] (with $T_n \equiv \Delta_{\Phi_n, \Psi_n}^{1/2}$, $T \equiv M^{1/2}$, $\Omega_n \equiv A \Psi_n$, $\Omega \equiv A \Psi$ while noting that $\dlim{w}{n \to \infty} T_n \Omega_n$ exists so that [ref:rem:operators_SRimpliesW] applies), it follows that $A \Psi \in \dom(M^{1/2})$ and

It holds that $\comm{\ssupp_{\Psi_n}} \to \comm{\ssupp_\Psi}$ strongly because $\comm{\ssupp_{\Psi_n}} = J \, \ssupp_{\Psi_n} J$ by [ref:lem:vonNeumann_commMsupport] and $\ssupp_{\Psi_n} \to \ssupp_{\Psi}$ strongly by assumption [ref:enu:vonNeumann_convergenceRelModOpA2]. Therefore, it follows that $\eta_n \to \eta$ strongly in $\MH$. Moreover, since

## Spatial Derivatives

{#sec:vonNeumann_spatialDerivative}

The relative modular operator $\Delta_{\psi, \varphi}$ generalized the modular operator $\Delta_\omega$ of a faithful normal functional $\omega \in \NF{\MFM}$, and [ref:sec:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperator] demonstrated that it always acts on the Hilbert space from the standard form representation. In this section, the spatial derivative operator, a generalization of the relative modular operator which was introduced by \textsc{A. Connes} in 1980 [cite:Connes80], will be constructed. It is defined with respect to a semi-finite normal weight $\varphi$ on $\MFM$ and a faithful semi-finite normal weight $\psi$ on $\comm{\MFM}$. The advantage of the spatial derivative over the relative modular operator is that it is defined in any representation space for $\MFM$, not just the one from the standard form representation.

### Weights

{#subsec:vonNeumann_weights}

As mentioned, the spatial derivative is defined with respect to a so-called normal weight on the commutant; this is, in a sense, an \enquote{unbounded normal functional} [cite:StratilaZsido19]. The definitions and results presented here can be found, for example, in [cite:Hiai21] or [cite:Stratila20].

## Definition: Weight [label:def:vonNeumann_weight]

Let $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ be a von Neumann algebra. A \bemph{weight} on $\MFM$ is a functional $\varphi : \PE{\MFM} \longto [0, + \infty]$ satisfying $\varphi(A + B) = \varphi(A) + \varphi(B)$ and $\varphi(\lambda A) = \lambda \varphi(A)$ for all $A, B \in \PE{\MFM}$ and $\lambda \ge 0$. Define the following set which is actually a left ideal of $\MFM$:

$$
_ \ .
$$

Then the weight $\varphi$ is called

- \bemph{faithful} iff $\varphi(A^\ast A) = 0$ implies $A = 0$ for any $A \in \MFM$;

- \bemph{semi-finite} iff $\MFN_\varphi$ is $\sigma$-weakly dense in $\MFM$;

- \bemph{normal} iff $\varphi(\sup_{i \in I} A_i) = \sup_{i \in I} \varphi(A_i)$ for any increasing net $(A_i)_{i \in I} \subset \PE{\MFM}$.

Analogously as for normal functionals, one defines the \bemph{support} of a normal weight $\varphi$ to be the smallest projection $\ssupp(\varphi) \in \PO(\MFM)$ such that $\varphi\bigl(\id_\MH - \ssupp(\varphi)\bigr) = 0$ [cite:Stratila20]. As in the previous case, it holds that $\varphi$ is faithful if and only if $\ssupp(\varphi) = \id_\MH$. Below, the following notation will be used:

$$
( ) ( ( ) ) \ .
$$

## Example [label:exa:vonNeumann_weights]

([cite:Hiai21])
Let $\MFM = L^\infty(X, \mu)$ for a $\sigma$-finite measure space $(X, \Sigma, \mu)$, and define $\varphi : \PE{\MFM} \longto [0, + \infty]$ by $\varphi(f) \ce \int_X f \diff \mu$. Then $\varphi$ is a faithful semi-finite normal weight on $\MFM$ with $\MFN_\varphi = \MFM \cap L^2(X, \mu)$. Next, consider $\MFM = \BO(\MH)$ for a Hilbert space $\MH$. Then the trace functional $\tr : \BO(\MH) \longto [0, + \infty]$, $A \longmto \tr(A)$, is a faithful semi-finite normal weight with $\MFN_{\tr} = \HS(\MH)$.

\begin{para}[The GNS-construction]{#para:vonNeumann_weightGNS}
([cite:Hiai21], [cite:Stratila20])
Similarly as for a positive linear functional on a $C^\ast$-algebra (\cf{} [ref:subsec:operatorAlgebras_GNS]), one can also perform a GNS-construction for a weight $\varphi$ on a von Neumann algebra $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$. Define the inner product $\braket{X, Y}_\varphi \ce \varphi(X^\ast Y)$ on $\MFN_\varphi$, and let $\MH_\varphi$ denote the completion of $\MFN_\varphi$ with respect to $\bdot_\varphi$. Furthermore, let $\eta_\varphi : \MFN_\varphi \longto \MH_\varphi$, $A \longmto \eta_\varphi(A)$, be the canonical injection. Since $\MFN_\varphi$ is a left-ideal of $\MFM$, and since

[equation:eq:vonNeumann_weightInequality]
$$
(X^ A^ A X) _ ^2 _
$$

for all $A \in \MFM$, $X \in \MFN_\varphi$, it follows that there exists a $\ast$-representation $\pi_\varphi : \MFM \longto \BO(\MH_\varphi)$ which is uniquely determined by $\pi_\varphi(A) \eta_\varphi(X) \ce \eta_\varphi(AX)$. This representation will be faithful if the weight $\varphi$ is faithful, and in this case one may consider $\MFM$ as a von Neumann algebra on $\MH_\varphi$.
\end{para}

The next theorem, taken from [cite:Hiai21], was originally discovered by \textsc{U. Haagerup} in 1975 [cite:Haagerup75b]. A proof may be found in [cite:Stratila20].

\begin{ntheorem}[Haagerup]{#thm:vonNeumann_Haagerup}
For a weight $\varphi$ on a von Neumann algebra $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$, the following properties are equivalent:

[equiv]

- $\varphi$ is normal;

- $\varphi$ is $\sigma$-weakly lower semi-continuous;

- $\varphi(A) = \sup \set{\omega(A) : \omega \in \NF{\MFM}, \omega \le \varphi}$ for all $A \in \PE{\MFM}$;

- $\varphi(A) = \sum_{i \in I} \braket{\xi_i, A \xi_i}$ for all $A \in \PE{\MFM}$, where $(\xi_i)_{i \in I} \subset \MH$.

\end{ntheorem}

The object to be introduced next is required for the construction of the spatial derivative operator; the terminology is borrowed from [cite:OP04].

## Definition: Lineal [label:def:vonNeumann_linealWeight]

Let $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ be a von Neumann algebra, let $\psi$ be a semi-finite normal weight on $\MFM$, and let $(\MH_{\psi}, \pi_{\psi}, \eta_{\psi})$ be the GNS-representation of $\MFM$ with respect to $\psi$. Define the \bemph{lineal} of $\psi$ to be the set

$$

$$

consisting of so-called \bemph{$\psi$-bounded vectors}; this terminology is due to the fact that $\norm{\eta_\psi(A)}_{\MH_\psi} = \psi(A^\ast A)^{1/2}$. Note that the lineal is a linear subspace of $\MH$. Furthermore, if $\psi \in \NF{\MFM}$ happens to be a normal functional on $\MFM$, then the lineal is given by

$$
D( , ) = \ : \ C_ > 0 \ A : _ ^2 C_ \, (A^ A) \ .
$$

The proof of the following result follows [cite:Hiai21] and [cite:Stratila20].

## Proposition [label:pro:vonNeumann_propertiesLineal]

In the terminology of [ref:def:vonNeumann_linealWeight], the following assertions hold true.

- The lineal $D(\MH, \psi)$ is invariant under the commutant $\comm{\MFM}$.

- If $\psi$ is assumed to be faithful, then $D(\MH, \psi)$ lies dense in $\MH$.

## Proof [label:eq:vonNeumann_vectorReprInLineal]

\tAd{} [ref:enu:vonNeumann_linealInvariant]. Let $\xi \in D(\MH, \psi)$ and $\comm{A} \in \comm{\MFM}$ be arbitrary. For all $A \in \MFN_\psi$, there holds

$$

$$

\tAd{} [ref:enu:vonNeumann_linealDense]. Let $P \in \PO(\MH)$ denote the projection onto $\clos_{\ndot} \bigl(D(\MH, \psi)\bigr)$. It will be shown that $P = \id_\MH$; the assertion then follows from [ref:cor:operators_characterizationPerp] [ref:enu:operators_densePerp]. First, observe that the invariance of the lineal under the commutant implies that $P \comm{A} P = \comm{A} P = \comm{A} P P$ for all $\comm{A} \in \comm{\MFM}$. This shows that actually $P \in \bicomm{\MFM} = \MFM$. Next, because $\psi$ is a normal weight, [ref:thm:vonNeumann_Haagerup] implies that $\psi = \sum_{i \in I} \omega_{\xi_i}$ for some family $(\xi_i)_{i \in I} \subset \MH$. For every $i \in I$, there holds $\xi_i \in D(\MH, \psi)$; this follows from the representation of $\psi$ and noting that for all $A \in \MFN_\psi$,

$$
_ ^2 = _ (A^ A) = _ _ ^2 \ .
$$

Therefore, $P \xi_i = \xi_i$ for all $i \in I$ by definition of $P$, and so one obtains that $\psi(\mathord{\id_\MH} - P) = 0$. As $\psi$ was assumed to be faithful, it follows that $P = \id_\MH$. (Note that the previous observation $P \in \MFM$ was used in order to apply the weight $\psi$ to the element $\id_\MH - P \in \PE{\MFM}$.)

The next result, mentioned but not proved in [cite:OP04], will be required down the line to establish another result which will find crucial application in [ref:ch:relativeEntropy].

## Lemma [label:lem:vonNeumann_linealVectorState]

If $\psi = \omega_\Psi$ is a vector functional on $\MFM$ induced by $\Psi \in \MH$, then $D(\MH, \psi) = \comm{\MFM} \Psi$.

## Proof

\pp{1.} Note that [ref:eq:vonNeumann_vectorReprInLineal] in the previous proof shows that the vector $\Psi$ is contained in the lineal of the state $\psi$ it induces, and since $D(\MH, \psi)$ is invariant under the commutant of $\MFM$ by [ref:pro:vonNeumann_propertiesLineal] [ref:enu:vonNeumann_linealInvariant], it follows that $\comm{\MFM} \Psi \subset D(\MH, \psi)$.

\pp{2.} Let $\xi \in D(\MH, \psi)$ be arbitrary, that is, $\norm{A\xi}^2 \le C_\xi \, \norm{A \Psi}^2$ for all $A \in \MFM$ by [ref:eq:vonNeumann_linealNormalFunctional]. Consider the subspaces $\MH_\Psi \ce [\MFM \Psi]$ and $\MH_\xi \ce [\MFM \xi]$ of $\MH$; they, as well as their orthogonal complements, are invariant under $\MFM$. Define a linear operator $\comm{T_\xi} : \MFM \Psi \longto \MFM \xi$ in $\MH$ by setting $\comm{T_\xi} (A \Psi) \ce A \xi$ for all $A \in \MFM$. The previous inequality shows that $\comm{T_\xi}$ is bounded, and that $A \Psi = 0$ implies $\comm{T_\xi} (A \Psi) = A \xi = 0$. Therefore, $\comm{T_\xi}$ is well-defined and extends uniquely to a linear operator $\comm{T_\xi} : \MH_\Psi \longto \MH_\xi$ ([ref:thm:operators_BLT]). Note that if $(A_n \Psi)_{n \in \N}$ and $(B_n \Psi)_{n \in \N}$ are two different sequences approximating the element $\eta \in \MH_\Psi$, \ie{}, $\dlim{\MH}{n \to \infty} A_n \Psi = \dlim{\MH}{n \to \infty} B_n \Psi = \eta$, then

$$

$$

so the definition of $\comm{T_\xi}$ is indeed independent of the approximating sequence. This establishes that $\comm{T_\xi} : \MH_\Psi \longto \MH_\xi$ is a well-defined bounded linear operator. Finally, since $\MH = \MH_\Psi \oplus (\MH_\Psi)^\perp$ ([ref:thm:operators_orthogonalProjection]), one can extend the operator $\comm{T_\xi}$ to the whole space $\MH$ by setting $\comm{T_\xi} \zeta \ce 0$ for all $\zeta \in (\MH_\Psi)^\perp$.

Let $A \in \MFM$ and $\zeta \in (\MH_\Psi)^\perp$ be arbitrary. As mentioned above, it holds that $A \zeta \in (\MH_\Psi)^\perp$ and, moreover, $A \comm{T_\xi} \zeta = 0 = \comm{T_\xi} (A \zeta)$ by definition of $\comm{T_\xi}$; this shows that $\comm{T_\xi}$ commutes with $A$ on the subspace $(\MH_\Psi)^\perp$. ### Intertwining Representations

As mentioned in the introduction of this section, the goal is to construct an analogue of the relative modular operator which can be employed in any representation of the von Neumann algebra. Therefore, it is fruitful to study how the GNS-representation intertwines with other representations.

The following proposition collects basic properties of $R_\xi^\psi$ and $\Theta^\psi(\xi)$ [cite:Hiai21].

\leavevmode

- For every $\xi \in D(\MH, \psi)$ and $\comm{A} \in \comm{\MFM}$, it holds that $R_{\comm{A} \xi}^\psi = \comm{A} R_\xi^\psi$.

- The operator $R_\xi^\psi$ intertwines the GNS-representation of $\MFM$ on $\MH_\psi$ with the identity representation $\MFM \owns A \longmto A \in \BO(\MH)$ of $\MFM$ on $\MH$: $A R_\xi^\psi = R_\xi^\psi \pi_\psi(A)$ for all $A \in \MFM$.

The following proposition shows that the spatial derivative is a generalization of the relative modular operator to the setting in which the von Neumann algebra $\MFM \subset \BO(\MH)$ is represented on an arbitrary Hilbert space $\MH$, not necessarily the standard representation [cite:Hiai21]. In particular, it follows that the examples from [ref:exa:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperator] also apply to the spatial derivative. The proof of the assertion may be found in [cite:Hiai21].

# The Araki-Uhlmann Relative Entropy

{#ch:relativeEntropy}

In the previous two chapters, the theory of operator algebras and modular theory in von Neumann algebras were outlined very roughly. Now, the focus of the presentation shifts towards applications of this theory to the study of the relative entropy functional. In [ref:sec:relativeEntropy_standardForm], the Araki-Uhlmann relative entropy is defined for von Neumann algebras in standard form, and its most important properties are proved. [ref:sec:relativeEntropy_spatialForm] discusses the same functional for arbitrary representations of the von Neumann algebra; both definitions are useful in different situations, and both will be employed in later investigations in this text. The main part of this chapter is [ref:sec:relativeEntropy_monotonicity], where Uhlmann's monotonicity theorem for the relative entropy is proved in great detail, and some of its corollaries are discussed. Finally, [ref:sec:relativeEntropy_vectorMonotonicity] contains some original results: Uhlmann's theorem is applied to the specific situation of two vector functionals in order to find monotonicity inequalities with respect to certain Hilbert-space transformations.

\begin{references}
The main sources are [cite:OP04] and [cite:Araki76, Araki77, Petz85, Petz86a].
\end{references}

## von Neumann Algebras in Standard Form

{#sec:relativeEntropy_standardForm}

In the following, a generalization of the Umegaki relative entropy, \cf{} [ref:eq:introduction_Umegaki], to normal functionals on general von Neumann algebras will be given. It will be assumed that the von Neumann algebra is represented in standard form (\cf{} [ref:sec:vonNeumann_standardForm]). In this case, the relative entropy was defined for faithful normal states by \textsc{H. Araki} in 1976 [cite:Araki76] using the relative modular operator (\cf{} [ref:sec:vonNeumann_relativeModularOperator]). Subsequently, in 1977 he generalized his formula to non-faithful states in the seminal work [cite:Araki77].

### Definition and Examples

## Definition: Relative entropy -- standard form [label:def:relativeEntropy_stdRelativeEntropy]

Let $(\MFM, \MH, J, \NPC)$ be a von Neumann algebra in standard form, let $\psi, \varphi \in \NF{\MFM}$ be two positive normal functionals, and let $\Psi, \Phi \in \NPC$ be the corresponding vector representatives of these functionals in the natural positive cone ([ref:thm:vonNeumann_vectorRepresentativesNormalStates]). The \bemph{Araki-Uhlmann relative entropy} of $\psi$ and $\varphi$ is defined to be

$$

## Remark [label:rem:relativeEntropy_stdRelativeEntropy]

The relation $\ssupp(\psi) \le \ssupp(\varphi)$ is equivalent to the condition $\Psi \in \supp(\varphi)$. Indeed, since $\supp(\psi) = \ran\bigl(\ssupp(\psi)\bigr) = [\comm{\MFM} \Psi]$ according to [ref:pro:operatorAlgebras_supportVectorFunctional], it is clear that the former implies the latter. For the converse implication, let $\xi \in \supp(\psi)$ be arbitrary, \ie{}, $\xi = \dlim{\MH}{n \to \infty} \comm{A_n} \Psi$ for some $(\comm{A_n})_{n \in \N} \subset \comm{\MFM}$. As the assumption $\Psi \in \supp(\varphi)$ implies $\ssupp(\varphi) \Psi = \Psi$ ([ref:lem:operators_rangeProjection]), one also obtains

$$

where in the second step $\ssupp(\varphi) \in \MFM$ was used, \cf{} [ref:para:operatorAlgebras_support]. This shows that $\xi \in \ran\bigl(\ssupp(\varphi)\bigr) = \supp(\varphi)$ by the aforementioned lemma, hence $\supp \psi \subset \supp \varphi$.

The following representation of $\MS_\MFM^std(\psi, \varphi)$ is given in [cite:Araki77] as a definition.

## Lemma [label:lem:relativeEntropy_spectralRepresentationRE]

Let $\MFM$, $\psi, \varphi \in \NF{\MFM}$, and $\Psi, \Phi \in \MP$ be as above. Denote by $E_{\Psi, \Phi}$ the unique spectral measure associated with the positive self-adjoint relative modular operator $\Delta_{\Psi, \Phi}$. In case that $\ssupp(\psi) \le \ssupp(\varphi)$, the relative entropy $\MS_\MFM^std(\psi, \varphi)$ can be written equivalently as

$$

Therefore, $\ssupp(\varphi) \Psi = \Psi$ by [ref:lem:operators_rangeProjection]. Using also $\ssupp_\psi \comm{\ssupp}_\varphi = \ssupp(\psi) J \ssupp(\varphi) J$ ([ref:lem:vonNeumann_commMsupport]), it follows that $\ssupp(\Delta_{\Psi, \Phi}) \Psi = \Psi$ because $J \Psi = \Psi$ since $\Psi \in \NPC$, see [ref:pro:vonNeumann_propertiesNPC] [ref:enu:vonNeumann_JonNPC].
